status: source repair proposed; no validation executed by worker
symptom: attempt-010 times out at TestRSVPNativeProducer native link-down facility repair; tunnel 93 never projects protection-in-use after primary LinkSetDown.

root-cause.mechanism: start subscribes to future link updates, seeds linkNames but leaves known empty. The first RTM_NEWLINK for an index emits created and returns before the up/down branch. For a pre-existing primary link, the first down update is swallowed by that return.
root-cause.confidence: Exact source defect. The retained native timeout and packet sequence are consistent with it, but attempt-010 has no event-bus capture proving the first update seen by this monitor.

related-caller-defect.mechanism: RSVP consumes interface/down in OnStarted but declares only fib-kernel and sysctl dependencies. OSPF loads interface in attempt-010; RSVP alone does not ensure its notification producer is loaded.

candidates.workaround: Prime the fixture with an extra primary link update before LinkSetDown, or synthesize an interface/down event.
candidates.source: Preserve the created event and emit the same RTM_NEWLINK current carrier state as well; declare interface as an RSVP dependency.
candidates.why-workaround-is-wrong: Priming hides the lost first carrier notification on every pre-existing interface and changes the fixture instead of repairing the producer.

ruled-out.prefix-match: Initial H capture has tunnel 93 RESV source and RSVP_HOP 10.11.0.2 on ifindex 9. acceptReservation stores src as NextHop; configuration assigns primary 10.11.0.1/24, so handleLinkDown would match primary before refresh convergence.
ruled-out.projection: showFastReroute emits tunnel-id and protection-in-use from the LSP ProtectionInUse field; the native oracle reads those exact fields.
ruled-out.bypass-selection: selectBypass selects configured a for merge-point 198.18.2.1. Both native private contexts were established and UDP was delivered before the failure trigger. No repair FIB failure or local-repair log appears in H output.

scope: Existing notification and caller dependency repairs only. No fixture, transport or RFC feature extension.
normative-claims: None. This diagnosis concerns the documented internal notification contract.
